rust/src/tests/process_crash.rs::recover: A child fills block 0 with the same byte and flushes it to a temporary volume.
Kill the child as soon as it confirms the flush, without letting it close the volume.
A new process must open the volume and read the entire pattern back.
A child writes six patterns across three blocks; some addresses receive more than one write.
Flush all six writes, wait for confirmation, then kill the child before it closes the volume.
After reopen, each block must contain its own last pattern, not the first pattern written to that address.
A child writes and overwrites blocks on a three-block volume, then flushes them.
Trigger an uncaught panic after the flush instead of closing the volume normally.
Reopening must return the final flushed pattern for each of the three addresses.
rust/src/tests/process_crash.rs::buffere: Give the engine enough buffer space to hold a single write without sending it to disk.
Kill the writer after the write in one run and after a flush in the other.
Only the flushed run must recover the new pattern; the buffered-only run must retain its earlier contents.
rust/src/tests/process_crash.rs::recover: The engine has saved an old value for block 0. A child process overwrites that block.
Kill the writer once the backing record has been written, before a client flush.
Recovery may return either complete value because the overwrite was not flushed. It must not return a mixture.
The engine has saved an old value for block 0. A child process overwrites that block.
Kill the writer after it updates the block location in memory but before a client flush.
Recovery may return either complete value because the overwrite was not flushed. It must not return a mixture.
The engine has saved an old value for block 0. A child process overwrites that block.
Request a flush and kill the writer immediately after the operating system finishes syncing the log.
Reopening must return the entire new value. Returning the earlier value is not allowed at this boundary.
rust/src/tests/process_crash.rs::crash_t: The crash-test planner offers a quick mode and a more extensive acceptance mode.
Ask it to schedule 339 possible interruption points in each mode, count repetitions, and supply an invalid mode.
Quick mode samples the first, middle and last points once. Acceptance selects all points and repeats scenarios twenty times. The invalid mode must fail.
rust/src/tests/process_crash.rs::recover: A child process flushes four writes to three blocks, then closes the volume. Close saves a new checkpoint: a map for recovery.
Kill the process just after it writes the new index page but before it publishes the checkpoint.
Recovery must use the older checkpoint and follow the later records to recover the last flushed value of each block.
A child process flushes four writes to three blocks, then closes the volume. Close saves a new checkpoint: a map for recovery.
Kill the process after it syncs the checkpoint records but before it writes the record selecting them.
Recovery must use the older checkpoint and follow the later records to recover the last flushed value of each block.
A child process flushes four writes to three blocks, then closes the volume. Close saves a new checkpoint: a map for recovery.
Kill the process just after it writes the descriptor that selects the new checkpoint, before the final sync.
Reopening the file must use the new checkpoint and return the latest flushed value for all three blocks. This is a process crash, not a power cut.
A child process flushes four writes to three blocks, then closes the volume. Close saves a new checkpoint: a map for recovery.
Kill the process immediately after the final sync of the descriptor that selects the new checkpoint.
Reopening the file must use the new checkpoint and return the latest flushed value for all three blocks. This is a process crash, not a power cut.
rust/src/tests/reclaim/descriptor_surviv: Two successive checkpoints describe the same flushed client data. Only the newer checkpoint allows the engine to reuse region zero.
Prepare separate disk copies with the newer checkpoint descriptor either absent or intact, then open both.
Without the descriptor, keep the region unavailable. With it, mark the region free. All eight client blocks must match in both copies.
rust/src/tests/reclaim.rs::overwrites_be: Repeatedly overwriting 80 client blocks generates more records than the file can hold at once.
Let the engine move current data and recycle regions occupied by obsolete writes.
Space must become available without losing the latest values. After reopen, live data must still occupy exactly 80 blocks.
rust/src/tests/reclaim.rs::entirely_dead: Successive writes leave a whole sealed region with no current data.
Let the storage cleaner release that region and request that the underlying file give back the space.
It must free the region without scanning it for copies or moving payloads that no client needs.
rust/src/tests/reclaim.rs::backing_disca: The engine can reuse space internally without asking the operating system to discard file storage.
Disable backing discard, then exercise space reclamation.
The engine must still reclaim space, with no backing discard requests issued and no discard failures.
rust/src/tests/reclaim.rs::relocation_ac: Two current blocks in one old region have their locations recorded on separate map pages. The cache holds two pages.
Change the intervening map page while waiting to move the two blocks.
The engine must copy both current blocks and preserve the intervening update. All four expected values must survive reopen.
rust/src/tests/reclaim.rs::relocation_sp: Two blocks due to move need different map pages, but the cache can hold only one page.
Request relocation while a third map page has an outstanding change.
Relocation must handle the moves in smaller units, copy both blocks, and preserve all four client values after flush and reopen.
rust/src/tests/reclaim.rs::user_overwrit: The cleaner has selected two blocks for copying but has not yet applied its plan.
Overwrite or discard one of those blocks before allowing the cleaner to continue.
It must reject the obsolete copy, copy the other block, and preserve the new value or zeros instead of restoring the old data.
rust/src/tests/reclaim.rs::proposal_from: Save a cleaner proposal for a sealed region. The proposal identifies which generation of that region it examined.
Free and reuse the same region, then submit the old proposal.
The engine must reject it even though the region number matches. The block map and current client data must remain intact.
rust/src/tests/reclaim.rs::fallback_to_t: A newer checkpoint allows an old region to be reused. A later log entry leads into that reused space.
Make the newest checkpoint unusable and reopen from the older one, which still lists that region as pending release.
Recovery must follow the later link, recognize that the region is open for writing, and recover the expected client values.
rust/src/tests/reclaim.rs::backing_growt: A volume can use whole new regions after its backing file grows.
Request growth, repeat a request for the same size, try invalid sizes, and reopen after changing the available file length.
New whole regions must become available exactly once. Repeating the same request must not append a record. Recovery must reject a file shorter than its required size.
rust/src/tests/reclaim.rs::growth_record: A child grows a backing file from five usable regions to nine after the original volume has saved a known block.
Kill the child just after it writes the growth record or just after it syncs that record.
Recovery must retain the block and see either the old size or the complete new size. Growth to nine must remain possible.
rust/src/tests/reclaim.rs::steady_state_: Open a volume and prepare its buffers before counting heap allocations.
Run reads, writes, and cleaning on that open volume while measuring allocations.
The measured operations must allocate no additional heap memory. At least one region must be freed, so the count cannot pass merely because the cleaner did nothing.
rust/src/tests/reclaim.rs::cleaner_follo: A cleaner must track regions added after the engine starts, including growth learned during recovery.
Grow the volume and drive writes and reclamation through the new space, testing both running and reopened volumes.
New regions must be usable; the cleaner must scan, move data and discard backing space without errors or losing expected client values.
rust/src/tests/reclaim.rs::pressure_publ: An old region contains metadata but no current client data. The running volume needs more space.
Drive further writes so space pressure forces the engine to publish an updated checkpoint.
It must free the old region without requiring a restart and keep the expected contents at the client addresses.
rust/src/tests/reclaim.rs::victim_left_w: An old region contains only metadata still used by the current checkpoint.
Run maintenance and publish a later checkpoint so that recovery no longer needs those metadata blocks.
The region must wait for safe release instead of requiring data copies. The client blocks must retain their expected values.
rust/src/tests/reclaim_crash.rs::relocat: A child repeatedly overwrites numbered blocks and periodically flushes while the engine moves data to reclaim space.
Kill the child at each selected step in moving records, linking regions, discarding space, or publishing a checkpoint.
Recovered blocks must match one consistent prefix of the write sequence without torn values. New writes and a flush must still work.
rust/src/tests/records_retry.rs::persist: The engine has retained copies of writes so that it can retry a failed flush.
Make both the first sync and the one permitted retry return input/output errors.
The client must receive the error. The engine must stop serving this volume and refuse a later flush rather than retry indefinitely.
rust/src/tests/records_retry.rs::discard: The engine has buffered enough information to replay recent writes but then receives a discard, which changes the valid data history.
Inject a sync failure at the next flush.
Do not replay the pre-discard history: return the error after one sync attempt and stop serving requests on the volume.
rust/src/tests/records_retry.rs::records: The memory reserved for replay copies is full. Accepting more writes would require dropping some retained bytes.
Submit the write that triggers an internal sync and make that sync fail.
The write must fail and the engine must stop rather than evict bytes it would need to make earlier writes durable.
Keeping replay copies requires both exclusive access to the backing file and space in the engine’s memory budget.
Try enabling retry with conflicting ownership, with too little memory, and when both requirements are met.
The engine must refuse unsupported configurations and account for the extra memory within its budget when it succeeds.
rust/src/tests/records_retry.rs::enablin: The engine accepts a write before the caller enables replay. Its retained copies therefore cover only part of the writes awaiting a flush.
Enable retry, add a write, then make the sync fail.
Return an error after one sync attempt. Replaying only the retained subset must not turn the incomplete flush into a success.
rust/src/tests/records_retry.rs::one_sho: A volume with retry enabled writes a known block and records the current log sequence number.
Let the underlying sync succeed but report an error once. Flush again after writing a different block.
Retry must not append another logical update for the first block. Service must continue and both complete patterns must survive reopen.
rust/src/tests/seeded_dst/plan.rs::v1_wi: Fault schedules can be saved and replayed; changing their text format could silently change the workload.
Generate the schedule for seed 42, compare it with fixed reference text, and feed the parser unsupported versions and invalid entries.
Valid text must round-trip unchanged. Invalid schedules must be rejected before the engine runs.
rust/src/tests/seeded_dst.rs::replay_fro: The caller supplies either a number that generates a repeatable workload or a saved list of writes and storage faults.
Run the specified plan against a temporary volume and compare the blocks in the recovery copy with the independently tracked writes.
Each scheduled fault must actually occur, and the recovered bytes must match. A missed fault or mismatched block must not pass.
rust/src/tests/seeded_dst.rs::generated_: Generate a fault schedule from seed 42, save it as text, and read it back.
Run both forms, then deliberately send a write to the wrong block and separately schedule a fault the workload will not reach.
Both normal traces must match. The checker must identify the wrong block and report the missed fault as inconclusive.
rust/src/tests/stale_tail.rs::recovery_a: Construct a sequence of valid records covering every supported number of data blocks per record.
Open the prepared backing file with the production recovery code and read each logical block.
Recovery must reach the last footer, count all record bytes, and return the final pattern at every address.
rust/src/tests/stale_tail.rs::rejects_in: The test builds a disk image with a valid prefix followed by a suspect record. A footer identifies which client blocks the record contains.
Give the footer a valid checksum even though it declares zero data blocks, then reopen the image.
Recovery must not apply this malformed record. It must stop at the last valid update and clear obsolete bytes instead of treating them as later client writes.
The test builds a disk image with a valid prefix followed by a suspect record. A footer identifies which client blocks the record contains.
Give the footer a valid checksum even though it declares more data blocks than the format permits, then reopen the image.
Recovery must not apply this malformed record. It must stop at the last valid update and clear obsolete bytes instead of treating them as later client writes.
The test builds a disk image with a valid prefix followed by a suspect record. A footer identifies which client blocks the record contains.
Give the footer a valid checksum even though it declares a position beyond its storage region, then reopen the image.
Recovery must not apply this malformed record. It must stop at the last valid update and clear obsolete bytes instead of treating them as later client writes.
The test builds a disk image with a valid prefix followed by a suspect record. A footer identifies which client blocks the record contains.
Give the footer a valid checksum even though it names a client block outside the volume, then reopen the image.
Recovery must not apply this malformed record. It must stop at the last valid update and clear obsolete bytes instead of treating them as later client writes.
The test builds a disk image with a valid prefix followed by a suspect record. A footer identifies which client blocks the record contains.
Give the footer a valid checksum even though it names the same client block twice, then reopen the image.
Recovery must not apply this malformed record. It must stop at the last valid update and clear obsolete bytes instead of treating them as later client writes.
The test builds a disk image with a valid prefix followed by a suspect record. A footer identifies which client blocks the record contains.
Give the footer a valid checksum even though it puts a nonzero block address in a slot declared unused, then reopen the image.
Recovery must not apply this malformed record. It must stop at the last valid update and clear obsolete bytes instead of treating them as later client writes.
The test builds a disk image with a valid prefix followed by a suspect record. A footer identifies which client blocks the record contains.
Give the footer a valid checksum even though it puts a nonzero checksum in a slot declared unused, then reopen the image.
Recovery must not apply this malformed record. It must stop at the last valid update and clear obsolete bytes instead of treating them as later client writes.
rust/src/tests/stale_tail.rs::recover_af: Opening a prepared volume finds an invalid gap followed by obsolete bytes that must be erased before new appends.
Kill the recovery process after selected batches of clearing writes, then open the same file again.
The engine must complete cleanup and recover the valid prefix without exposing records beyond the gap.
Recovery clears obsolete bytes after a break in the log and syncs its cleanup writes.
Kill the process just after that sync, inspect the cleared range, and open the volume again.
The affected bytes must already be zero, and a second recovery must still recognize only the valid updates.
rust/src/tests/stale_tail.rs::invalid_ga: Prepare two open storage regions with an invalid gap and bytes that could look like later records.
Open the volume to trigger recovery and inspect the remaining space in both regions.
Recovery must stop at the gap, preserve earlier valid data, and clear the obsolete tails rather than accepting later bytes as writes.
rust/src/tests/stale_tail.rs::stale_tail: The backing file contains three whole regions and five extra blocks too short to form another region.
Write a valid record followed by marker bytes, then reopen the volume and inspect the file.
Recovery must clear the unused tails of the two open regions but leave the free region and the five trailing blocks unchanged.
rust/src/tests/volume_write.rs::multiple: Several logical addresses on a temporary volume receive distinct data patterns.
Read each address while the volume is open, then close it, reopen it and read each address again.
Each read must return that address’s complete pattern rather than zeros or the pattern for a neighboring block.
rust/src/tests/volume_write.rs::repeated: A client writes several values to the same block in sequence.
Read the block after each overwrite and reopen the volume after the last write.
Each live read must show the newest value at that point. After reopen only the final value should remain visible.
rust/src/tests/volume_write.rs::overwrit: A client block already contains nonzero data.
Overwrite the block with zeros, read it immediately, then close and reopen the volume.
Both reads must return zeros throughout the block. An older nonzero value must not reappear during recovery.
rust/src/tests/volume_write.rs::raw_foot: The engine appends writes in a single storage region; each record ends with a footer identifying its place in the log.
Inspect the raw footers written to the backing file instead of relying only on client reads.
Sequence numbers must advance in order and each footer must point to the correct previous and current positions.
rust/src/tests/volume_write.rs::log_full: A small volume has no usable space left for another record.
Try another write and compare the block map and backing data with their previous contents.
The write must report no space without replacing the last successful value. The engine must remain usable and return the earlier value after reopen.
rust/src/tests/volume_write.rs::out_of_r: A valid block already holds a known pattern, and the engine has recorded its location and checksum.
Try to write outside the logical volume and inspect the map and next write position.
The engine must reject the address as invalid without advancing the log, changing the map or damaging the original block.
rust/src/tests/volume_write.rs::write_bl: A fresh volume has space for a new client write.
Write one patterned block and inspect both the raw data record in the file and the location the engine publishes for the block.
The stored bytes must match the payload. The identifying footer, position, sequence and checksum must agree with the mapping.
rust/src/tests/volume_write.rs::failed_w: Make the backing file inaccessible for writing while the engine still holds a volume open.
Attempt to write a client block and inspect the map, log position and later operations.
The write must fail without publishing a mapping or advancing the log. The engine must refuse further operations rather than confirm a write it did not store.
rust/src/tests/volume_write.rs::public_o: Start with a new two-block volume and use its public read, write, flush and close operations.
Read an unwritten block and an invalid address, save a pattern, reopen it, then corrupt one saved byte in the file.
Unwritten data must read as zero, the invalid address must fail, and the pattern must survive reopen. After corruption, reading must fail without changing the caller’s buffer.
rust/src/tests/write_buffer.rs::releases: The engine groups buffered blocks into records with a maximum payload count.
Write batches ranging from a single block to 676, including counts near the record boundary. Flush, close and reopen each volume.
Every logical address must return its own pattern even when saving the batch required more than one record.
rust/src/tests/write_buffer.rs::release_: Give the engine a buffer for 340 client blocks; each on-disk record also needs a footer identifying its data.
Write 340 different blocks, flush, and inspect the engine’s size and occupancy counters.
It must count two records containing 338 and two blocks, two footers, and less than one percent extra space for footers.
rust/src/tests/write_buffer.rs::duplicat: Three writes to the same block fit in one in-memory batch.
Overwrite block zero three times, inspect the log position, then flush.
Nothing should reach the log before the flush. The flush must consume only one data block plus its footer, and the client must read the third value.
rust/src/tests/write_buffer.rs::read_aft: The volume can hold an entire write in memory before flushing it to the backing file.
Write a known pattern and read it back before issuing any flush; also read an unwritten block.
The client must see the buffered pattern immediately and zeros at the unwritten address.
rust/src/tests/write_buffer.rs::enospc_i: On a small volume, buffered writes could promise more space than the log can supply.
Write distinct addresses until the first no-space error, testing both small and large buffer settings. Flush and reopen.
The write that cannot fit must fail immediately. All accepted writes must survive; the rejected address must read as zero.
rust/src/tests/write_buffer.rs::checkpoi: A large logical volume needs two index pages to locate its block maps.
Write different patterns near the beginning, in the middle of the populated addresses, and at the final address. Close and reopen.
Both index pages must exist. Each written address must return its own pattern, and an unwritten address must still read as zero.
rust/src/tests/write_buffer.rs::short_ba: The engine can accept a write into memory before it knows whether the backing file can store it.
Replace the backing file handle with a read-only handle. Buffer a write, then flush it.
Flush must report a bad file descriptor, not a successful partial write. The mapping and sequence number must not advance, and subsequent writes must fail.
